title: Tom Archer's ballrooms and Lawrence Welk's trailer band
summary: The Tom Archer agency books a string of Midwest ballrooms; Leeman recalls following Lawrence Welk's six-piece polka band, which lived in a trailer and paid $75 a week.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Sioux City. Now we worked -- the agency used to be Tom Archer, and I still think he might be alive or some of his relatives -- Tom Archer. He used to hire the territorial bands, and he used to have a whole string of ballrooms, some of them were out in the prairie; Sioux City, Iowa, Sioux Falls, Pipestone, Minnesota and Kansas City, which I'll get to -- we haven't got there yet -- and Lincoln, Nebraska, we had to play in a sandstorm.

This Tom Archer -- his ace in the whole was a six-piece orchestra and was called Lawrence Welk, doing one nighters -- 7 one nighters a week, and they made hundreds and hundreds of thousands of dollars; they were sold out playing polkas, and we would follow them with our appetizing 13 or 14-piece hokum band, they used to call them in those days.
Now what year is this? We just mentioned Boston in 1933 -- is this still ...
Lawrence Welk had a band in 1933?

Oh, yes. Yes. He was the biggest thing -- it was his ace in the hole out there. I remember it was '33 or '34. I went back the next year, they had those long trailers and he was the first person to put thousands of dollars in a big trailer, and they lived in it -- his six-piece orchestra, and they would do seven days a week all over the midwest, for this Tom Archer. And I remember we were flabbergasted, they had showers in there, they had bunks -- and I heard at that time that he paid his men $75 a week, and that was unheard of in those days. I think you have some ideas of your own about what pay was in those days.
Oh, I agree. I was in California in 1933.
So that was the band that we went down to Kansas City with, which was the biggest thing that could have happened to me in life.
